criteria.statement: A config.json that exists at the real path but is unreadable (permission-denied) or is a directory rather than a file produces a refusal reason distinguishable from 'file absent' (already covered by C8/C11) -- first-boot (registry never configured) must read differently from a corrupted/inaccessible later state, since an operator's remedy differs (create vs. fix permissions/restore). Deliberately scoped as this component's own ablation/negative-control criterion for REQ-76, discharged at implementation per PDP.md section 3's design-scope clarification (real ablation fixtures at implementation, not a non-author prose falsification pass at this stage) -- not left implicitly deferred to a stage that may never open for this addition.

All three reasons must differ from each other in the audit event, not collapse to one generic 'config invalid' string.

failure_criteria.statement: A guard fails open on the path that matters: any availability-matrix row, dependency outage, clock anomaly, or malformed input lands ALLOW or silent-skip instead of a named DENY/refusal.
failure_criteria.detection: Every deny/refusal path has a test asserting it rejects with its named reason; the C6 fail-open mutant battery is a PERMANENT suite fixture run on every pass (the toy-d2 lesson: absence and error are where fail-open hides) -- a change that lets the mutant pass is a regression.

failure_criteria.statement: A number appears with no reproduction path -- in particular an AI-3 proposed value taking effect through code, config-without-valid-decision-record, or payload.
failure_criteria.detection: C8/C11's behavioural refusal probes (no input yields a value while config is invalid) -- deliberately not source greps, which int('1800') and 60*30 defeat.

failure_criteria.statement: Code assumes a path exists that this component does not create: dispatch-records dir, sessions.jsonl, the ingested-copy tables, config.json, the decision-record file.
failure_criteria.detection: Every externally-owned path failure is an exercised probe (C4, C6, C8, C11) -- checked by test, not by startup assumption.

failure_criteria.statement: A deny or divergence is written to a channel nobody reads: registry-unavailable sub-reasons that never reach the gate audit event, a two-plane disagreement logged instead of ticketed, or a replay-detected orphan line silently reconciled.
failure_criteria.detection: C6 asserts sub-reasons in the audit event payload; C10 asserts a finding object; C14 asserts the orphan line surfaces as a divergence event.

failure_criteria.statement: A clause satisfied by string presence rather than resolution: evidence checked by shape without ledger resolution, component matched on payload strings without target resolution, dispatch record read from the payload's own claims, or config validity read from its own fields.
failure_criteria.detection: C1's self-asserted and scope-mismatch probes, C2's fabricated/replayed probes, C3's resolution probe, and C11's hash-mismatch probe stay in the suite permanently; a change that makes any of them pass is a regression, not a simplification.

failure_criteria.statement: config.json's absence, corruption, or inaccessibility all produce the same undifferentiated refusal reason, or a permission/directory-shape failure is not distinguished from simple absence.
failure_criteria.detection: C17's three-fixture ablation battery -- each of absent/directory/unreadable must assert its own distinct reason string.

out_of_scope: The two claude-hooks-v2 hooks (gate client registration, registry write guard) -- chv2's to build and register; this component ships the read/write library they call.
AI-3's lease and window values -- operator decision; this component reads them from a hash-verified decision record and refuses without it.
AI-4's permission-binding mechanism and the per-dispatch secret of 34.7's impersonation disposition -- consumed when they exist, not built here.

Interface-level end-to-end criteria (registry_to_ingest ingestion, gate-client wiring in a live hook, tessera CLI finding emission E2E) -- .foreman/GOALS.integration.json, owned by foreman:integration-test.

ATLAS's tenth-source ingestion of the registry and both JSONLs, and trigger-1 query EXECUTION on the analytics plane -- the ingest/analytics side; this component ships emissions and the query definition (C11).
Graduated responses (DENY/ASK/annotated-ALLOW) -- deferred at architecture (34.9), must not arrive as an implementation-stage souvenir.
Multi-repo reconciliation aggregation policy beyond parse+diff+localize, and the ticket-emission write itself -- integration scope.
An evidence-set (multi-act) table -- named future additive migration; v1 is single-act by stated design (schema doc, finding 5).
constraints: stdlib + sqlite3 only, matching the repo's existing components; no new dependency.
Registry reads stay off the per-tool-call blocking path (34.2's budget statement); any design putting them there re-measures against that path's own standard.
One SQLite file, journal_mode=WAL (decided, schema doc finding 8, with the missing-sidecar residual named there); spent_ref lives inside registry.db for clause-(b) transactionality.
The component never self-registers hooks; enforcement wiring is chv2's, consultation-side validation (34.7 clauses a-d) carries the load.
Schema changes are additive migrations bumping user_version (C15); the evidence_class CHECK widens only by migration, never by code interpreting the field loosely.

ALLOW's meaning is the schema doc's stated limit (finding 4): act + authority authenticated, outcome attested by the dispatch-accountable verifier, revocation as correction -- no consumer may document a stronger claim.
Field-level schema is DESIGN-REGISTRY-SCHEMA-AI5-ATLASSN-110-20260912.md (post-muse-2 revision); divergence between that doc and DDL is a defect in whichever moved without an amendment here.
